activeBuild.brief: Two fresh isolated Three.js builders rebuilt only the frozen ticks 29, 34, and 41 animation presentation from exact baseline afc1063812473087a645271e2c33adcd0534225a. A source-blind selector chose Builder B by 57–56 while disqualifying both from AAA selection. Root integrated the stronger candidate, passed the full technical gate, froze commit fc74f4e4c74c3dcac422461546854cdc3b7da3b0, and handed that exact game state to a fresh independent critic.
facts: P00 is accepted as infrastructure; its blind visual baseline remains an explicit 28.33–76.67 loss.
P10 remains paused after rejected Round 017 and the unfiled Unity Round 018 stop; it is not the active browser-work lane.
Round007 is rejected at 34/100 with 0/3 focused, 0/6 overall, and 0/10 categories at the required 9/10 floor.
Round008 fanned the same bounded FX assignment to two fresh isolated builders from exact baseline 2cb09a9b8f496d24f93a05dd351051cd89351329.
A fresh read-only selector chose Builder B because its localized impact burst and directional slash contour made S04 contact more immediately readable; it explicitly did not claim benchmark quality.
Root integrated Builder B at production commit 7e88906a168489938ae500ed5cb317b71a312970 and froze critic target 5359f91bad13fe83e70169231e519911a8fbebc4.
Only CharacterViews.ts and CombatFx.ts differ from the Round007 baseline; the other 25 tracked production source files are byte-exact.
Root reproduced all six selected Round008 frames byte-for-byte and passed every one of 16 technical gates before critic handoff.
A fresh independent critic checked out exact commit 5359f91bad13fe83e70169231e519911a8fbebc4 in isolation and recaptured six headed Chrome 150 RGB frames from the actual production game.
The critic sealed randomized mapping first, sealed anonymous scores before reveal, and then rejected Round008 at 39.3/100.
Round008 won 0/3 focused combat comparisons and 0/6 overall comparisons; no category reached the required 9/10 floor.

Category scores are character 3.2, environment/material 3.8, lighting/color 3.4, camera/composition 5.0, combat pose/readability 5.5, motion FX/readability 3.6, UI 4.0, depth/atmosphere 3.2, animation/physical credibility 4.5, and overall AAA finish 3.1.

Every capture and runtime validity gate passes: exact commit, Node 24 clean install, tests and build, production serve, headed WebGL2, 1600×900 DPR 1, 18/18 assets, no fallback, no errors, focused determinism, lifecycle, and context restore.
Supplemental visual telemetry still fails the C01 blade safe frame and C06 player-height gate; those are visual composition failures, not capture invalidity.
The critic named exactly one gap: ticks 29, 34, and 41 read as disconnected pose samples instead of one physically coherent sword-contact force chain.
Round009 fanned that single gap to two fresh isolated builders from exact baseline afc1063812473087a645271e2c33adcd0534225a.
Builder A filed physically grounded weight transfer at f95fd2942fc0f60dc803ec433a3d10f7a581fc41; Builder B filed forceful anime-cinematic physicality at ede933054c327d2b10c6a683cad99f22a799632f.

Both builders ran the actual production game at 1600×900 DPR 1, passed deterministic focused captures, 18 authored assets, zero fallback, tests, build, stability, resource caps, and context restoration.
A fresh selector saw only anonymous tick 29, 34, and 41 frames plus the matched benchmark references; it scored Builder B 57/100 and Builder A 56/100 after reveal.
The selector explicitly disqualified both candidates: tick 34 still reads as broad blade/FX penetration and tick 41 reads as an overhead re-windup rather than same-direction recovery.

Root integrated Builder B, passed Node 24 clean install, typecheck, lint, 18 unit tests, build, and four serial production-browser tests, then froze critic target fc74f4e4c74c3dcac422461546854cdc3b7da3b0.
A fresh independent Round009 critic is now recapturing the exact frozen production game and will seal randomized mapping and anonymous scores before reveal.
Repository-wide LFS integrity also fails on eight historical PNG blobs, although all 18 runtime assets are real bytes.
The global latest capture manifest remains intentionally pinned to accepted P00.

pieces.name: Evidence spine
pieces.outcome: A deterministic review scene, fixed-seed capture command, manifest, round ledger, and live progress surface work end to end.

pieces.name: Shoulder camera
pieces.outcome: Exploration and combat framings preserve subject scale, sightline, collision, target legibility, and authored camera presets.

pieces.name: Ground locomotion
pieces.outcome: Walk, run, pivot, stop, strafe, slope handling, and camera-relative control have grounded acceleration and readable weight.

pieces.name: Hero animation foundation
pieces.outcome: Idle, locomotion, pivots, combat stance, weapon handling, additive aim, and transitions share coherent body mechanics.

pieces.name: Light combo
pieces.outcome: Buffered three-hit chain has authored startup, active, recovery, and cancel windows with one-hit-per-target resolution.

pieces.name: Heavy attack
pieces.outcome: Heavy strike communicates commitment, displacement, contact, hitstop, camera impulse, and enemy reaction.

pieces.name: Dodge and evasion
pieces.outcome: Directional dodge, invulnerability window, recovery, and camera continuity are predictable and readable.

pieces.name: Hit reaction and death
pieces.outcome: Zombies react by hit direction and severity, preserve contact, stagger, collapse, and settle without foot sliding or explosive ragdolls.

pieces.name: Zombie navigation
pieces.outcome: One zombie can acquire, approach, flank, telegraph, attack, recover, lose or reacquire, and die without navigation jitter.

pieces.name: Crowd combat director
pieces.outcome: Four-to-six zombies surround without dog-piling; attack tokens, spacing, off-screen pressure, and threat cues create readable crowd combat.

pieces.name: Hero look development
pieces.outcome: Paused after rejected Round 017 and the unfiled Unity Round 018 stop. The historical look-development evidence remains preserved, but this is no longer the active implementation lane.

pieces.name: Zombie look development
pieces.outcome: The zombie archetype and variants have layered anatomy, clothing history, damage language, silhouette variation, and material response.

pieces.name: Arena composition
pieces.outcome: A compact arena has foreground framing, combat stage, silhouette depth, traversal logic, landmarks, and no empty test-level read.

pieces.name: Lighting and atmosphere
pieces.outcome: Key, fill, rim, exposure, fog, shadows, grading, and local reactive light keep faces and contact readable while creating depth.

pieces.name: Combat VFX
pieces.outcome: Weapon trails, contact flash, sparks, debris, blood or dust, and lingering particles form a restrained macro, impact, and decay stack anchored to motion.

pieces.name: Combat audio
pieces.outcome: Foley, effort, weapon movement, contact, zombie vocals, ambience, music, ducking, and spatial mix support timing and impact.

pieces.name: HUD and threat language
pieces.outcome: Minimal health, ability, lock-on, and threat information remains legible without weakening the cinematic frame.

pieces.name: Finisher vignette
pieces.outcome: A contextual finisher has reliable setup, three-character blocking when relevant, facial and contact framing, camera choreography, and clean return to play.

pieces.name: Integrated encounter
pieces.outcome: A polished 45–90 second encounter combines the accepted systems into one authored dramatic arc.

pieces.name: Performance and delivery
pieces.outcome: The native macOS target runs reliably, captures deterministically, meets frame budgets, and ships with reproducible build instructions.

pieces.name: Fighter contract
pieces.outcome: Data-driven fighter, weapon, and ability definitions support selection without branching the shared combat core.

pieces.name: Fighter two
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Roster select and persistence
